props.raw: Software Development using AI

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools

Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

props.title: Environment Setup and Configuration Parsing
props.exercise: Set up the local development environment, configure the AI coding agent framework, and parse configuration files to identify active components.
props.notes: Focus on understanding the configuration structure before writing code.

props.title: Implementing Custom Tools and MCP Bindings
props.exercise: Implement a custom local file-search tool and register it with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to extend agent capabilities.
props.notes: Requires local testing of MCP tool schemas.

props.title: Configuring Agent Skills and Bindings
props.exercise: Configure and bind custom tools to a code-refactoring agent, ensuring the agent can invoke them correctly during local refactoring tasks.
props.notes: Verify that no configuration warnings are reported.

props.title: Refining Skills and Specification Templates
props.exercise: Refine agent skills for complex refactoring tasks and translate a natural language use case into a structured specification template.
props.notes: Transitioning from agent configuration to specification development.

props.title: Constructing Executable Specifications
props.exercise: Construct executable specifications for an authentication module using spec-driven development patterns based on natural language requirements.
props.notes: Ensure all use cases in the requirements document are covered.

props.title: Automated Test Case Generation
props.exercise: Generate automated test cases from the executable specifications constructed in the previous week and verify they execute without errors.
props.notes: Focus on eliminating syntax and runtime errors in generated tests.

props.title: Mid-Semester Catch-up and Open Lab
props.exercise: Open lab session for catch-up, debugging previous lab exercises, and mid-semester exam preparation. No new content is introduced.
props.notes: Mid-sem exam week. Used exclusively for catch-up and review.

props.title: Tracing Execution Logs and Tool Loops
props.exercise: Trace execution logs of a coding agent and analyze the tool-calling loop to identify state divergence during a failed file-write operation.
props.notes: Analyze divergence between internal state and environment response.

props.title: Debugging State Divergence
props.exercise: Debug state divergence in failed file operations by analyzing execution traces and correcting the agent's tool-calling parameters.
props.notes: Focus on resolving the exact point of failure in file operations.

props.title: Setting Up Evaluation Pipelines
props.exercise: Set up and run an evaluation pipeline to compare the performance of two different AI-native software development workflows.
props.notes: Compare workflows quantitatively using reliability criteria.

props.title: Designing Multi-Component Workflows
props.exercise: Design and implement a multi-component web application workflow using an AI-native software factory setup.
props.notes: Begin work on the final project implementation.

props.title: Workflow Assessment and Justification
props.exercise: Assess and justify the reliability of the designed AI-native workflow against automation requirements, producing the final project deliverable.
props.notes: Justify design decisions against stated reliability requirements.

props.title: Project Presentations and Evaluation
props.exercise: Final project presentations and evaluation of the AI-native software development workflows.
props.notes: Peer evaluation and final grading of projects.
